newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent rangebound, awaits direction.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent rangebound, awaits direction.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+Brent is likely to trade within its recently established range with good resistance again at $18.64.
+Over the next few sessions, the outlook is up and the gap is likely to be filled.
+Gas oil is well supported and will remain within its $160-$167 boundaries.
IPE Brent crude oil and gas oil futures are expected to remain within their recently established ranges on Monday, traders and technical analysts said.

June Brent closed 14 cents a barrel lower on Friday at $18.27 after failing again at resistance at $18.64, the bottom of a chart gap dating from the beginning of the month. Shortly before the London open, it was quoted 10 cents off at $18.17. May gas oil ended Friday 75 cents up on the day at $165.50.

"Today the market is going to be very quiet, the market will be waiting for new information," said Wong Hui Ming at CA Global futures. "This is a very good time to write options, too, as there is likely to be low volatility."
He said that over the next few sessions, however, the market was likely to rise through the chart gap and test $19.26.
"Overall the stochastics are also vey good and the momentum is holding on the positive side, it is not oversold."
Peter Sceats at CharTech-MCS said the recent sideways trading had now brought the price action near to a falling four-month downtrend line on the continuation chart.

"If price can mount a settlement above $18.40 on Monday, or $18.30 on Tuesday and so on, the trend will have been properly challenged and the odds on follow through action to the upside will shorten."
On the June contract chart, however, "which broadly speaking carries less weight than the continuation chart," the top of the chart gap at $18.77 will continue to remain a bearish focus, he said.
"The least conservative version of the downtrend we could find looks to cross the price action at $19.00 on Monday, $18.96 on Tuesday, $18.92 on Wednesday and so on.
"While price is below this key trend line we have to assume the down trend (in the medium term) is ongoing," he said.
Wong said he saw gas oil trading again between $160 and $167 a tonne, a range by now well established.
MeesPierson Derivatives in London, using their Market Profile technique, also saw support at $163.50.
"Preparation is neutral and resistance seems clear at the range highs of $167," their daily report said.

"We look to trade this range responsively but probably look to buy first as a break of the range would be more likely on the upside at the moment and heating oil has maintained its support over the weekend."
-- Nicholas Shaxson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8167
